items.title: Released Dave response budget G = 5 min (25 blocks) is below Ethereum finality (65-96 blocks): an operator acting only on final history is charged on every response and loses by timeout after a few forced matches
items.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 released clock constants (Deployment.s.sol _getInclusionBudget, ClockBudgets, Clock.pauseAfterResponseAt)
items.role: Referee model, as the deployed referee
items.severity: Medium (preferred: section 3 'only changes how long a claim may take to respond ... rated as support', stood-in A7 Critical) / Critical (if Dave's clock sizing is the deployed referee's own decision, as preferred for R1-A7-1) / Low (if a confirmation-depth dispute policy counts as 'final')
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: not excluded; the A1-A8 exclusion keeps it because the referee model's own released constants violate A7; no reorg or early action needed - section 4 'The honest operator acts only on history that its policy treats as final, such as finalized blocks'. 2 Role: Dave = Referee model ('Audit the released constants'); section 3 'A defect that only changes how long a claim may take to respond ... is rated as support'. 3 Support stand-in: 'Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role'. 4 Alternative: A7 'No rule of the referee may make the honest claim lose by timeout while it acts within its own clock' and R4 'submits its transactions within the dispute clocks' violated on the honest path -> Critical. 5 Low if the recipe's depth-4 policy is a valid 'final' policy. Verified by reading: _getInclusionBudget returns 5 minutes; pauseAfterResponseAt charges elapsed - G; Dave's docs/dimensioning.md says responses 'read latest'.
items.reason: Dave's own docs say responses read 'latest'; section 4 makes the honest operator act only on final history, so every response overruns G. Referee-model clock sizing: support Medium (section 3), Critical alternative (A7), Low if shallow policy is 'final'.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7's released deployment fixes the per-response budget G = 5 minutes on every chain (bugs/harness/work/dave/released/prt/contracts/script/Deployment.s.sol _getInclusionBudget ~l.225; ClockBudgets.sol maxAllowance = C + 2G + (L-1)(T+2G), C = 1 week mainnet / 8 hours testnet). Clock.pauseAfterResponseAt (src/tournament/libs/Clock.sol:148-161) stores allowance - max(elapsed - G, 0) and reverts CannotAdvanceTimedOutClock once allowance <= elapsed; nothing refunds the excess. On Ethereum, G = 25 blocks while finality is 65-96 blocks. Dave's docs/dimensioning.md:42-60 states the budget works because a joined match's responses 'read latest'. THREAT_MODEL section 4: 'The honest operator acts only on history that its policy treats as final, such as finalized blocks ... Acting on history before it is final ... is outside this model.' So an operator that answers each bisection turn as soon as the turn is final is charged >= 41 blocks per response. Required behavior: A7 'The dispute constants and clocks leave room for the honest claim to play the logarithmic number of matches that a tournament forces on it ... No rule of the referee may make the honest claim lose by timeout while it acts within its own clock'; R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks'. Trigger: Sybil root claims (bonds only) paired one after another with the honest commitment (Dave's join pairing, see dropped R8-GOALTIMEOUT-2: a correct survivor re-dangles and meets every newly released Sybil), each answering instantly and abandoning on its last turn. Hunter's arithmetic (clocksim.py re-implementing ClockBudgets and pauseAfterResponseAt): testnet constants (G=25, T=600, C=2400, A=3100 blocks) expire the honest clock in forced root match 2 at lag 80/96 and match 3 at lag 65; mainnet in match 27/34/47. Test idea (hunter): bugs/<ID>/test.sh on the local chain with the released Dave build (unpatched): deploy CanonicalTournamentParametersProvider with the released testnet arguments and a factory, instantiate a root, join the honest commitment and a synthetic Sybil (trees differing at a chosen leaf, as Dave's tests build them); mine 65 blocks (one finality delay) before each honest advanceMatch, let the Sybil answer in the next block; when the Sybil abandons, claim the timeout and release the next Sybil. Assert the honest clockAllowance never drops below what it needs / advanceMatch never reverts CannotAdvanceTimedOutClock; expected exit 1 by match 2-3 on testnet constants. Rating to record: Medium (support rating of referee-model clock sizing) / Critical (A7) / Low (if a confirmation-depth policy counts as final). Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r8/GOALTIMEOUT/clocksim.py and hunt-GOALTIMEOUT.json candidate 1.

items.title: Dave's asynchronous pairing lets Sybils force a number of matches on the honest claim linear in the claims, where the manual and A7 assume logarithmic
items.role: Referee model, as the deployed referee
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: the pairing difference is a listed, non-normative simplification: manual 'In Dave ... Each claim that joins meets the one waiting, and a claim that joins late may meet one that has already won a match. The model gathers a tournament's claims first and runs the bracket in rounds' (doc/README.md ~11310); section 5 'The simplifications that the manual lists for it are not normative'. 2 Role: referee model; match count affects only response time (section 3 support). 3 No case. 4 No rule violated by the count alone: Dave discounts every action by G/T, so an operator within its budgets is never charged; R12 lets honest work grow with 'matches of the epochs still open'. 5 Low. Its multiplier effect is folded into R8-GOALTIMEOUT-1's brief.
items.reason: The linear count follows from the manual's listed non-normative simplification (claims meet 'the one waiting'); alone it charges no honest clock (section 5, R12). Low; noted as a threat-model gap in A7/section 7.

items.title: Vouchers above ~55 KB (all outputs above ~0.4-1 MB) can never be executed: executeOutput costs ~290 gas/byte plus calldata, while the rollup interface lets a guest commit outputs up to the 2 MiB tx buffer
items.component: cartesi-rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 Application.executeOutput/_executeOutput/LibBytes.consumeBytes4 (pinned by Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7); libcmt emit_voucher bound; manual rollup interface
items.role: Referee model, as the deployed referee (output validation)
items.severity: Critical (if A5's converse covers executing a committed voucher under the chain's per-transaction limits) / Medium (manual-behavior contradiction on a security-relevant point) / Low (if acceptance means validateOutput/validateOutputHash, which work for any size, and voucher size is the application's choice)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: section 2's correctly designed application constrains only the rollup interface and mcycles; nothing documents an output-size bound, so the application exclusion does not clearly apply; 'Keeping outputs to prove them later is not on the honest operator's path' excludes operator storage, not referee acceptance. 2 Role: Application output validation = Referee model ('rated as if a deployed referee had it'). 3 No listed case (constant-factor case is for R12 operations). 4 A5: 'Conversely, the referee accepts every output that the settled state commits to, whenever its valid proof is presented. No party can make it stop accepting them' -> Critical if execution is acceptance; section 8's 'honest proof or transaction that cannot fit' arguably covers it (no A3-like exemption for outputs). 5 Low if validateOutput (view, works at any size) is acceptance. Verified: consumeBytes4 copies byte by byte; validateOutput/validateOutputHash exist.
items.reason: A5 converse ('accepts every output ... whenever its valid proof is presented') vs no output bound matching executeOutput's gas/calldata limits; reading of 'accepts' decides Critical vs Low; manual contradiction gives Medium.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: a correctly designed application may emit a voucher or delegate-call voucher of any length up to the 2 MiB CMIO tx buffer (libcmt v0.18.1-test1 src/rollup.c cmt_rollup_emit_voucher/emit_delegate_call_voucher fail only with -ENOBUFS; emulator AR_CMIO_TX_BUFFER_LOG2_SIZE = 21; the manual's rollup interface states no other bound). The settled state commits to it, but the only effective acceptance of a voucher, Application.executeOutput(bytes output, OutputValidityProof) (bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/dependencies/cartesi-rollups-contracts-3.0.0-alpha.10/src/dapp/Application.sol l.163-184 -> _executeOutput -> src/library/LibBytes.sol consumeBytes4 per-byte copy loop -> abi.decode copy), costs about 290 gas of execution per output byte, and the calldata costs at least 40 gas per nonzero byte under the EIP-7623 floor. Under EIP-7825's 2^24 per-transaction gas cap every voucher above ~55 KB is unexecutable (hunter's forge measurements on Dave's released Application artifact with a mock validator: 53,380 B -> 15.87 M execution gas, 57,476 B -> 17.14 M, 131,204 B -> 39.6 M, 2 MiB -> ~0.82 G); independently of the copy loop, calldata alone exceeds 2^24 gas above ~419 KB nonzero (merged R8-GOALNOPROOF-1: anvil --hardfork osaka, N=418,000 nonzero bytes mined at 16,741,000 gas, N=420,000 stays pending) and geth/reth's 128 KiB txpool limit above ~126 KB. Inputs have A3's bound ('It accepts no input so large that the honest proof of its delivery would exceed the chain's per-transaction limits'); outputs have none. Required behavior (rule quoted): A5 'Conversely, the referee accepts every output that the settled state commits to, whenever its valid proof is presented. No party can make it stop accepting them.'; section 8 Critical 'An honest proof or transaction that cannot fit the chain's per-transaction limits, other than the delivery proof of an input that A3 requires the input record to refuse'. Trigger: an input makes a libcmt application emit a large voucher (e.g. payload echoed or aggregated from inputs); after settlement executeOutput with the valid proof cannot be included. Test idea (hunter): bugs/<ID>/test.sh runs a forge test like /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r8/GOALOUTPUT/gas/test/Gas.t.sol against the released Application artifact (bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/out/Application.sol/Application.json) with a mock IOutputsMerkleRootValidator (or a real height-63 outputs root built with cartesi.hash-tree), emitting a voucher of the largest size libcmt accepts or a 64 KiB witness; assert total gas (execution + max(standard intrinsic, EIP-7623 floor)) <= 2^24 and calldata <= 131,072 bytes; exits 1 today. Fixed behavior: an execution path that fits every output the interface allows, or a documented and enforced output-size bound (libcmt refusing, manual stating it) that the test then checks. Record rating Critical / Medium / Low with the deciding question: does A5's 'accepts' cover executing a voucher under per-transaction limits, or only validateOutput (a view that works at any size)? Evidence: hunt-GOALOUTPUT.json candidate 1, hunt-GOALNOPROOF.json candidate 1.

items.title: Forked PRT player computes claims in whatever cartesi-jsonrpc-machine PATH names, while version checks measure the in-process library; JSON-RPC client checks only protocol 0.9
items.component: PRT player forked mode (doc/recipes/prt.lua new_machine/new_forked_player); jsonrpc_machine::check_server_version
items.role: Support (PRT player); JSON-RPC client machine API
items.rating_steps: 1 Not excluded by trigger alone. 2 Role: support stand-in for the honest operator. 3 The stood-in High case 'A node that cannot detect a version mismatch' does not hold: new_machine loads the template into the spawned server (prt.lua ~997-1001), and the server's machine load runs validate_processor_shadow (src/machine.cpp:205-217), which refuses a template whose marchid, mvendorid or mimpid differs from the server build. R13 requires each STF-changing version to change these registers, and R1-R13-3 found no identification collision involving the audit/prt2 build (the hunter's 'marchid 23 for all v0.23 pre-releases' contradicts R1-R13-3's evidence: v0.23.0-test2 has marchid 22). A server of another released version fails loudly. The remaining client-vs-deployment gap is R1-A6-2. 5 Low.
items.reason: Claim of silent divergence is false for released versions: the server's load-time validate_processor_shadow refuses a template of another marchid/mvendorid/mimpid (src/machine.cpp:205-217); residual is R1-A6-2/R1-R13-3 territory.

items.title: AMOs translate their address twice (read walk then write walk): one AMO can load from one physical page and store to another, sets PTE.A on a store page fault, loses PTE.D on its own PTE; failed SC sets PTE.D
items.component: Interpreter execute_AMO / execute_SC with translate_virtual_address (native, uarch program, collectors, log producers)
items.severity: Medium (preferred: undocumented deterministic deviation consistent across paths) / Critical (literal R7: 'Address translation and memory permissions' and 'Atomics and fences' are listed areas where 'any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest')
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: trigger is guest execution in a reproducible machine; no exclusion applies (the guest-subversion exclusion requires R7 to hold). 2 Role: interpreter = Honest operator. 3 Medium case 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)' if (a) needs a missing sfence.vma, (c) a self-mapping PTE, and spurious A/D only perturbs aging. 4 Literal R7 in two listed areas at a reachable state -> Critical (same split as confirmed R1-R7-1). Verified by reading: execute_AMO calls read_virtual_memory then write_virtual_memory (src/interpret.cpp ~1358-1379), each with its own TLB lookup and walk; failed SC calls write_virtual_memory<skip_write>.
items.reason: Code confirms two independent translations per AMO and a store-type walk on failed SC; R7 lists address translation and atomics. Medium (no correct guest relies) / Critical (literal R7), as for R1-R7-1.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: src/interpret.cpp execute_AMO (~l.1358-1379) performs an AMO as read_virtual_memory<T, STATE_ACCESS, true>(vaddr) followed by write_virtual_memory<T>(vaddr, result); each consults its own TLB set (read vs write) and on a miss runs its own translate_virtual_address walk (src/translate-virtual-address.hpp), each walk updating A/D after its own permission check. execute_SC's failed path (~l.1314-1330) runs write_virtual_memory<T, write_mode::skip_write>, whose walk sets PTE.D though nothing is stored. The RISC-V A extension defines an AMO as one access that loads and stores 'back to the original address', translated once as a store/AMO access (privileged spec 4.3.2: permission check at step 5 before any A/D update at step 7; updates must be exact). Manifestations observed by the hunter on native and uarch with identical root hashes: (a) with a stale read-TLB entry V->P1 and a write-TLB entry V->P2 (PTE changed without sfence.vma, write TLB refilled by a store), amoadd.d returns P1's 100, leaves P1 unchanged and writes 101 into P2 (was 200); (b) an AMO on a leaf PTE with R=1, W=0, A=0 raises store/AMO page fault (mcause 15) but sets A (PTE 0x20244803 -> 0x20244843); (c) an AMO on the PTE word that maps its own page (A=0, D=0, W=1) writes back the value read after only A was set, clearing D (PTE ends 0x20200847, should be 0x...c7); failed SC (rd=1, no store) sets D (0x20244c47 -> 0x20244cc7). Required behavior (rule quoted): R7 'The emulator implements the RISC-V specification ... departing only where the manual documents a deviation ... In these areas, any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest, even a deviation that is consistent across all paths: ... Address translation and memory permissions. Atomics and fences.' The manual documents no deviation here. Trigger: guest code at S or M (with MPRV) under Sv39 paging; reachable from any valid template (section 2: any assignment of guest-writable memory and registers is presumed reachable). Test idea (hunter): bugs/<ID>/test.lua builds /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r8/GOALESCAPE/amo.c with bugs/harness/baremetal/build.sh into a 64 MiB bare-metal machine, runs to halt and asserts: (a) either (P1==101 and P2==200) or (P1==100 and P2==201), with rd equal to the old value of the updated location; (b) after the faulting AMO, mcause==15 and the leaf PTE's A bit still 0; (c) after the self-PTE AMO, PTE has A and D set; optionally failed SC leaves D clear. Also check run_uarch per mcycle against the native root hash so the fix keeps paths in agreement. Decide per manifestation whether the spec really forbids it (e.g. whether spurious A/D on a faulting AMO or failed SC is permitted by the Svade/Svadu text in the pinned spec version) and keep only assertions the spec requires; (c) and (a) are the strongest. Driver: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r8/GOALESCAPE/amo.lua. Rating to record: Medium (preferred) / Critical (literal R7), as R1-R7-1.

items.title: PRT bridge accepts and settles any staged epoch result without comparing it with its own final state, raises no alarm during staging, then crash-loops crisium after acceptance
items.component: doc/recipes prt-bridge.lua methods:jobs (acceptStagedTournamentResult), prt-epoch.lua poll asserts, crisium.lua
items.role: Support (PRT player/bridge), stands in for the honest operator
items.rating_steps: 1 Trigger: a non-honest root winner, which under the goal's assumptions (honest operator acting within the clocks) needs another defect or a violated assumption; that other defect is what to rate. 2 Role: support stand-in for the honest operator. 3/4 In the stood-in role no rule is violated: acceptStagedTournamentResult is permissionless, so the bridge's call adds nothing an adversary could not do; no rule requires the operator to alarm during staging; the Medium alternative rests on the guardian's reaction window, a trusted deployment role outside the model (R1-A5-1 reading). 5 Low.
items.reason: Precondition is the honest claim losing, impossible under the goal's assumptions; accepting is permissionless; alarm during staging is required by no rule and relies on the guardian, a role outside the model (R1-A5-1). Low.

items.title: DaveConsensus never registers the template's outputs root: template-committed outputs are refused until epoch 0 is accepted (forever if foreclosed first); EpochSealed(0) reports a zero outputs root
items.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 cartesi-rollups/contracts DaveConsensus (constructor, isOutputsMerkleRootValid, acceptStagedTournamentResult) with rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 Application.validateOutput
items.role: Referee model, as the deployed referee
items.severity: Critical (literal A5: 'A valid template is such a state' and the referee accepts its outputs 'whenever its valid proof is presented') / Low (delay only, if 'settled state' means one settled by a tournament or non-genesis templates are unsupported; the permanent foreclosure variant is out of scope as the guardian is a trusted deployment role)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: the foreclosure variant needs the guardian (trusted, R1-A5-1 reading) -> out of scope; the delay variant needs no guardian and is not excluded (the referee model itself fails A5, 'unless an implementation of the referee model is what violates it'). 2 Role: DaveConsensus = Referee model, 'rated as if a deployed referee had it'. 3 No listed case. 4 A5 'An outputs Merkle root is defined only for a settled canonical state that waits at a manual yield with the accepted reason. A valid template is such a state' + 'Conversely, the referee accepts every output that the settled state commits to, whenever its valid proof is presented' -> Critical at the deployment's initial state. 5 Low if a one-epoch delay is not a refusal or non-genesis templates are unsupported (open gap, see R2-DFOUTPUT-1). Verified: _outputsMerkleRoots written only at DaveConsensus.sol:272 (acceptStagedTournamentResult); constructor emits EpochSealed(0, ..., bytes32(0), ...) at :145; Application falls back to TEMPLATE_HASH (Application.sol:442) for the last finalized machine root.
items.reason: Code confirms the template's outputs root is never registered; A5 makes the valid template a settled state whose outputs must be accepted 'whenever'. Critical literal / Low as a delay or if non-genesis templates are unsupported.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: DaveConsensus (bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/src/DaveConsensus.sol) writes _outputsMerkleRoots only in acceptStagedTournamentResult (l.272); the constructor (l.116-145) seals epoch 0 from initialMachineStateHash and emits EpochSealed(0, 0, upper, initialMachineStateHash, bytes32(0), tournament) without registering the template's outputs root; isOutputsMerkleRootValid (l.398-406) therefore returns false for it. Application (cartesi-rollups-contracts-3.0.0-alpha.10 src/dapp/Application.sol) validateOutput/validateOutputHash (l.328-350) revert InvalidOutputsMerkleRoot, while its own _getLastFinalizedMachineMerkleRoot falls back to TEMPLATE_HASH (l.442), i.e. treats the template as the finalized state. Required behavior (rules quoted): section 2 valid template: 'Its tx buffer holds the outputs Merkle root of every output that the application accepted before it, which at genesis is the root of the empty outputs tree'; A5: 'An outputs Merkle root is defined only for a settled canonical state that waits at a manual yield with the accepted reason. A valid template is such a state.' and 'Conversely, the referee accepts every output that the settled state commits to, whenever its valid proof is presented. No party can make it stop accepting them.' Trigger: deploy a Dave application (DaveAppFactory.newDaveApp(templateHash, ...)) from a valid template whose tx buffer holds a non-empty outputs root R (e.g. the harness bare-metal emit-output template after one accepted input); before epoch 0 is accepted, call Application.validateOutput(output0, proof against R). Expected today: revert InvalidOutputsMerkleRoot. Do NOT rely on guardian foreclosure for the permanent variant (the guardian is a trusted deployment role per R1-A5-1's outcome); the test should show the refusal of a valid proof at the deployment's initial settled state, and may additionally show that it lasts at least the whole first tournament plus the staging period. Note: the recipe player refuses such templates (R2-DFOUTPUT-1), so use the released (unpatched) Dave build directly with forge or the local chain. Test idea (hunters): forge test on the released build deploying DaveAppFactory/DaveConsensus with that template hash and asserting validateOutput succeeds right after deployment; exits 1 today, 0 once the constructor registers the template's outputs root (e.g. from a machine validity proof of the template). Rating to record: Critical (literal A5 at the initial settled state) / Low (delay only, or non-genesis templates not supported; see gap 'Genesis vs non-genesis templates' in AUDIT_REPORT.md). Evidence: hunt-GOALEPOCH.json candidate 2, hunt-GOALOUTPUT.json candidate 2.

threat_model_gaps: Chain finality vs dispute responses (R8-GOALTIMEOUT-1): section 4 says the honest operator 'acts only on history that its policy treats as final, such as finalized blocks', under a heading about the 'input policy'. The model does not say whether this binds observing match moves and responding, nor whether a confirmation-depth policy counts as 'final'. Dave's released G (5 min) assumes responses read 'latest'.

Number of forced matches (R8-GOALTIMEOUT-2): A7 and section 7 assume 'the logarithmic number of matches that a tournament forces', and R12 sizes per-match costs by it. The manual's listed, non-normative simplification (Dave pairs each joiner with the waiting claim) lets Sybils force a linear number. The model does not say how A7 sizing applies when the deployed referee forces more matches than the normative bracket.

Output acceptance vs execution and size (R8-GOALOUTPUT-1, R8-GOALNOPROOF-1): A5's converse ('accepts every output ... whenever its valid proof is presented') does not say whether acceptance includes executing a voucher under the chain's per-transaction limits, or only validating it (validateOutput works at any size). Section 8's Critical entry on proofs or transactions that cannot fit has an A3 exemption for inputs but no counterpart bound for outputs, and does not say whether output-execution transactions sent by parties other than the honest operator count.

Template as settled state (R8-GOALEPOCH-2, R8-GOALOUTPUT-2): A5 says 'A valid template is such a state', but also 'The settled state is the last leaf of the winning claim'. It is unclear whether the template counts as the settled state before epoch 0 is accepted, and whether a delay in accepting its outputs breaks 'whenever'. This extends the existing genesis/non-genesis template gap (R2-DFOUTPUT-1).

Withdrawal path (R8-GOALNODE-1): the AUDIT table names the rollups contracts' 'input box, output validation' only. Neither the AUDIT table nor the threat model covers the foreclosure/withdrawal path (accounts-drive proofs). R9's 'lost lengths' covers only 'every tree the emulator defines', not data-to-node length binding of application encodings checked by a referee contract.

Operator behavior after a divergent settlement (R8-GOALEPOCH-1): no rule says whether the honest operator must keep defending later epochs from a settled state that differs from its own (A1 makes the on-chain settled state the next before-state), or may stop. No rule says whether it must signal during the staging period.
